decisions.reason: As a newly launched reusable crate that fits the firm's core sustainable packaging direction, management is likely to continue it and can still view any early weakness as temporary despite only modest public commitment so far.
The foldable large container sits close to the firm's core offer and having its own webpage signals visible commitment, which under escalation of commitment makes withdrawal within a year unlikely.

This stackable plastic crate matches the established reusable logistics business, and after only a short time on the market management would be inclined to give it more time rather than reverse course.

The medium-duty rackable pallet is strongly aligned with the firm's pallet and transport-packaging capabilities, so sunk development effort and strategic fit support retention despite limited public prominence.
Because the spill-retention pallet received a dedicated webpage and extends the firm's pallet range in a credible way, management would be reluctant to drop it so soon after launch.
The plastic pallet with load retainers is highly central to the firm's packaging portfolio and was publicly presented on its own page, making continued commitment the most likely choice.
